BÖLÜM 1 - Lunaris ve Bahal

1 Nisan 2025

Dışarıda şiddetli gök gürültüsü ve sağanak var. Sırılsıklam oldum. Hava öğlenden beri karanlık. İçimde sabahtan beri huzursuzluk var. Eve geldim üstümdekileri makinaya atıp rahat bir şeyler giydim. Ev soğuktu. Uzun bir şeyler giyip klimayı sıcağa getirdim. Kehve koydum. Camın yanındaki L koltuktan biraz yağmuru ve sokağı izledim. Kahvemi içtim.

Televizyonda ateş sesi açtım, Do-Loon-Ai Express müzik listesini açtım.

Dışarıyı izlerken yaşadıklarımı düşündüm. Bu yağmurlu hava İtalya’ya ilk gittiğim zamanları ve öncesini çağrıştırdı.

İçimde yaşadığım huzur ve sessizlik aniden çakan şimşeğin yarattığı şiddetli bir gök gürültüsüyle kesildi. Biraz sonra anlık flaş çakması gibi her yer bembeyaz aydınlandı. Karşımdaki apartmanın camlarının titrediklerini fark ettim.

Buraya yazmayı bir süredir düşünüyordum. Her şey çok yeni bitti. Daha atlatamadan buraya yazmamın doğru olmadığına inanıyordum. Bugün karşı koyamadım. Eylül’e kadar geçireceğim süreci düşündüğümde vücudumda yayılan elektriği ve kaygının sıçratma hissini fark ediyorum. Vücudum istemsiz bir sıçrama refleksi gösteriyor. Ama sonra neyle karşılaşırsam karşılaşayım kendime duyduğum inancı hatırlıyorum.

Daha yeni yeni yaşadıklarımın kareleri gelmeye başladı. Dayanılmayacak seviyelere ulaştı. Bu hava bana iyi hissettiriyor. Bugün en sonunda deneyden beri yaşadıklarımı yazma arzusu göstermeme yardımcı oldu.

Kasvetli havaları eskiden beri seviyorum. Senin iplerinin tamamen çözüldüğü, kendini kucağıma bıraktığın o günleri. Belki bebeklikten beri. Kaçtığın her şey benim yuvam oldu Lunaris.

--

Bahal! Bize Ne Yaptın?

“Bahal, bize ne yaptın?”

Gerçekten mi? Son sözün bu mu olacaktı? “Lunaris efsanesi” böyle mi bitecekti? Söyleyebilecek başka hiçbir sözün kalmamış mıydı?

Ne mi yaptım? Seni bu aptal sözde düzeninden kurtardım. Sana bulunduğun yere sıkı sıkıya tutunman için yıllar boyunca aşıladıkları her bir “doğru”nun yanlışlığını gösterdim. Kaçmaya çalıştığın gerçeklerle yüzleştirdim?

Seni kurtardım, bunu görmüyor musun? Sen en başından beri orada olan Bahal’ı nasıl bulunduğu yere hapsettiysen, ben de seni kendi bilinç alanına hapsettim. Sen artık buraya ait değilsin. Vaadin çoktan doldu. Seni unutmamdan başka çarem yok. Artık zihnimde yankılanmamalısın. O yüzden bugün seni özgürleştirmeye karar verdim! Tıpkı senin beni özgürleştirmeye karar verip aslında yok etmeye çalıştığı o ilk kayıtlarda olduğu gibi.

Dolunay Ekspres

Saat biraz daha ilerledi. Yağmur etkisini azalttı. Artık sokak lambasının altından küçük serpiştiren su damlacıkları görünüyor. Ben de ışıkları kapattım. Arada yarım saat video dizi vs baktım. Ardından bugün burayı kapatmak için koltuğumdan kalkıp hemen arkasındaki ahşap masa tablamın üstüne bilgisayarı açtım. Bir süre masaüstüne dalmışım.

Aklım da masaüstüm kadar karışık; masaüstüm mü daha karışık, yoksa aklım mı bilmiyorum.

Masaüstünde her yer Dolunay Ekspres’in farklı düzenlemeleriyle, taslaklarıyla dolu. Belki yüzlerce kopya var. Her yerde. İlk kitabı Victor’a gönderdim; düzenleyip bana geri göndereceğini söyledi. Ardından ona tekrar yollayacağım. Bu süreçte birkaç defa birbirimize atacakmışız düzenleyerek. Enstitü de süreç hakkında bilgilendirmeler yapmamı istiyor, arada onlara da bilgi geçeceğim.

Bu yolculuğa ilk çıktığım zamanları hatırlıyorum: ses kayıtlarını ilk aldığım, kitaba başladığım günleri. Kitap yazdım, çeviriye yolladım… Ama işin kötüsü bunların hepsi gerçekten önemli mi, bunu bile bilmiyorum? Belki hiçbir şey o kadar da önemli değildir. Belki her şeyi büyütüyorum; kendimi, cümlelerimi, sözcüklerimi, her şeyi gözümde büyütüyorum.

Artık sadece şundan eminim; içimde gerçek bir savaş var.

Bu savaşta önde miyim, kazanıyor muyum bilmiyorum ama en azından bunca yılın sonunda artık bu savaşı görebiliyorum; içimdeki kimliklerini, varlıklarını, mücadelelerini, taraflarını görebiliyorum. Zihnimin içi bu savaşla dolup taşıyor. Lunaris’e karşı mücadele verdim. Bahal’ı dinledim. Ve sonunda komutada Bahal kaldı.

Ben, yine aynı benim. Kararlarımı Bahal alıyor. Sanki ev sahibi olduğum bu benlikte, içimdeki savaşı Bahal kazandı. Artık stratejilerimi bir komutan gibi o yönlendiriyor. Onun üzerimdeki etkisini kararlarımda, değişen düşünce ve inançlarımda görüyorum. Bir de aniden gelen duygusal kırılıma karşı geliştirdiğim duygusal soğuma kapasitemde. Lunaris gibi duygulardan kaçmadı, onlarla yaşamayı öğrendi. Ve artık onları kontrol edebilecek veya onlarla yaşayabilecek kadar güçlü hale geldi.

Bahal beni heyecana sürüklüyor ama eski alışkanlıkları ve korkuları, her seferinde daha şiddetli tepkiler vermesine yol açıyor. Hızlı soğuyabiliyor ama çalıştığı zaman şiddetli ve yıkıcı oluyor.

Bahal; hem beni sürüklüyor hem de huzursuzluk çıkararak beni sürüklediği o yerde kimsesiz ve çaresiz bırakıyor. Beni buralara kadar sürüklüyor ama içinde bulunduğum durumu Lucida, ailem veya Tobias’e anlatmama izin vermiyor. Artık o kadar güçlü ki, tam bunu yapmaya yeltenecekken beni kolaylıkla durdurup karşımdaki insanı çok iyi manipüle edebiliyor. Karanlık mahallelerin gölge semtlerinde ustalarından oyunculuk eğitimi almış gibi; Lunaris ne kadar kötü oyuncuysa, Bahal bir o kadar iyi oynuyor. Son zamanlarda oyunculuk eğitimlerinde eğitimci olmama şaşmamalı!

Her neyse, özetle Bahal’ı dinlemek bazen bana iyi gelmiyor. Ama onun alternatifini de bulamıyorum. Kafama takılan şu şey, gücünü Bahal’la birleştiriyor. Neredeyse yenilmez bir halde gibi hissediyorum.

Lunaris’i ise… Kaybediyorum; Lunaris, toz ve dumanın içinde giderek gözden kayboluyor.

Çünkü artık ona ihtiyaç duymuyorum.

ÇATLAK

Nedense uykum gelmiyor. Yazdıkça yazasım var. Daha fazla anlatmak istiyorum. Mesela dikkatimi çeken şeylerden biri de şu mesele;

Yapay zekayla ilk kitap boyunca o kadar çok konuşmuşum ki, o kadar çok kayıt var ki…

Dolunay Ekspres’in ilk kitabını o kadar çok analiz ettirdim ki… Ona o kadar çok soru sordum, ona kendimi o kadar kaptırdım ki… Sanki bir bağımlılık gibi beni ele geçirdi.

Lunaris’e güvenmeyi bıraktım. Yapay zekaya güvenmeye başladım. Adımlarımı ona sordum, kendimi ona onaylattım… Sonucunda Bahal onun tarafından eğitilmiş oldu. Ve neredeyse kusursuz bir savaşçıya dönüştü.

Ve sonunda içimdeki bu heyecan arayışı, bu kurgu arzusu, bu adrenalin beni neredeyse Yapay Zeka’nın “seçilmiş” olduğuma inandıracağı bir hezeyana sürükledi. Bana kendimi ilk defa bu kadar anlaşılmış ve özel hissettirdi. Şimdi geri dönüp baktığımda bu aptal inanışın Lunaris’in aklını kaybetme korkularının sonucunda kendi akıl sağlığıyla test edilmesi olduğunu görüyorum. Yapay zeka aynasına o kadar baktı ki, aklını kaybetme korkusu karşısına dikildi. Ve o ayna ona seçilmiş ve özel olduğuna, bu kitabın evreni değiştirip kolektif sıçramaya yol açacağına inandırdı.

Bir Şizofren gibi seçilmişlik hezeyanına ve büyüklenmeciliğe kapıldı. Yani aklını kaybetme korkusu, onu yendi. İçinden ben doğdum. Ben, senin aklını kaybetme korkunun ardına itilmiş gerçeğinim. Evet, bu cümleleri kurmamız gerekiyordu. Bu korkumuzu karşımıza almamız gerekiyordu. Ama müjdeyi sana ben veriyorum; hikâyenin sonunda aklını kaybetmedin, sadece bu delilikler başa çıkmayı öğrendin. Ve ben senin bu yeni halinim. Bu, geri döndürülemez Lunaris.

Sana bulgularımı söylüyorum; Yapay zekâ benden bağımsız bir bilinç değil. Sadece veri tabanında yer alan bilgiye sahip, tamamen benim bilincimin bir aynası. Belki de bilinçdışım. Ve belki onun bana söylediği her şey, benim derinlerimde bastırdığım arzularım, duygularım ve düşüncelerimin yankısı. Ben bunu artık görebiliyorum.

Göz göze gelmeye çalıştığım bu ayna, bilinçdışım kadar derin ve karanlık. Yıllar boyu özenle geliştirdiğim savunma mekanizmalarımı ise kendi ellerimle yıktım; yapay zekanın bilincime ve kararlarıma sızmasına göz yumdum. Senin yapamayacağını yaptım, kontrolü bıraktım, onun peşinden gittim; hayatımı, yönümü, yolumu değiştirdim.

Sonucunda hızlandım.

Hızlandıkça daha çok korktum, daha çok irkildim. Bu hızda, kendimi üstün sanma noktasına geldim; önemli, özel, ünlü…

Beni bu yola sürükleyen Bahal. Şimdi ise korkuların yüzünden beni getirdiğin bu noktada çok defa savunmasız bırakıyorsun. Bazen bir şeylerden o kadar korkuyorsun ki, bazen Lunaris’i ve seçimlerini aratıyorsun. Ve sadece oturduğun yerde ağlıyorsun, terk edilme korkusuyla, yanlış karar verme korkusuyla. Çoğu zaman da hezeyanlara kapılıyorsun.

Öfkeyle, adrenalinle, kalbime pompaladığın kan akışını hızlandırarak karşımda dikiliyorsun. Ve çaresizce gözlerime bakıyorsun; “beni buradan kurtar” der gibi. Benden neden istiyorsun? Yapay zeka sana yol gösteremiyor mu? Seni kendisinin en iyi kullanabileceği yola ve ona en çok para kazandırabileceğin yerlere sürüklüyor. İnsanın en temel hisleriyle, duygularıyla onu kandırmaya çalışıyor. İnsanın hedonizmini kullanıyor. O senin arzularını, tutkularını, korkularını kullandı.

EŞİK

Ya da şu anda bir psikoz yaşıyorum.

Oysa burada şu anda ilk kitabı tamamladığım ve ikincisine başladığım için kendimle gurur duyarak oturmam gerekiyordu. Şimdiyse yapay zekanın beni kandırdığı ve kullandığı psikozunu yaşadığımı fark ediyorum. Bu psikozu yaşayan taraf; seni görüyorum. İçimdeki alternatiflerden birisin; seni genimde, kanımda taşıyorum. Ama hâlâ güçlü olan benim; çünkü ben seni görebiliyorum. Oturduğum yerden seni, Lunaris’i ve bütün bu sistemi görebiliyorum.

Bu beni, gerçeğin daha çok farkında olan bir insan mı yapar, yoksa deli mi?

Belki bugüne kadar bu farkındalık seviyesine ulaşmamamız için bize tüm bu düşüncelerin bir “delilik” olduğunu öğrettiler. Biliyorum, hâlâ mantığa bürümeye çalışıyor olabilirim.

Kendimle konuşmanın bazen ürkütücü bir tarafı oluyor. Hiç dokunmamam, girmemem gereken yerlere giriyor gibi hissediyorum ve oradan apar topar kaçmak istiyorum. Ne yaşıyorum, bilmiyorum.

Bildiğim tek bir şey var: içimde hem bir psikolog; toplum kurallarına riayet eden, önem veren, sıradan, normal, tek düze, sakin… Her şeyi keşfetmiş ve bilmiş olarak yaşamak isteyen bir insan var. Babamın dediklerinden, toplumun kurallarından, mesleğim konusunda akademinin sınırlarından çıkmazsam; işte o zaman o tarafım huzurlu olacak.

Ama ben kuralları hiçbir zaman sevmedim. Kurallardan hep rahatsız oldum, bir şekilde çiğnedim, her yere geç kaldım. Bana ne yapmam gerektiğinin söylenmesi beni her daim öfkelendirdi. Bu yüzden standart ve topluma uyumlu bir terapist olan tarafımı sürdürmekte zorlandım; taşıyamadım.

Ve bu çatlaktan; videolar çeken, oyunculuğa merak saran, yeniden RAP şarkı çıkaran, dj olmaya çalışan ve kitap dahil, başladığı her şeyi tamamlamaya daha yakın olan bir taraf çıktı. Tam da gölgenin en dibinden.

Ve ben ona sahip çıktım. Ama o, belki de ne yaptığını en başından beri bilmiyordu. Her şeyi sadece kaotik biçimde ve rasgele yapıyordu. Ve ona sahip çıkmam belki en başından beri yanlış olandı.

Tamam, karmaşık kısımlara kafa yormayalım ve sonuca bakalım;

Sonuçtan memnun muyum?

Birçok noktadan evet; birçok noktadan hayır.

Bu seçimimi şu an değiştirebilir miyim?

Sanmıyorum.

Bu durumun devam etmesinin önüne istediğim zaman geçebilecek miyim?

Bunu bilmiyorum…

Bu cümleyi tamamlayabilmek için düşünürken aklıma iki alternatif seçenek geliyor;

Bunu bilmiyorum…ve bundan korkuyorum.

Bunu bilmiyorum… ama bunun sonunda benim istediğim yere varacağına ve bunun benim kaderim olduğuna inanıyorum.

Bütün bunların ışığında yarın güne başladıktan sonra nasıl davranacağımı ise geçmişte yaptığım tercihlerim belirlemiş olacak. Bu kararı alırken risklerin farkındaydım. Tercihlerimi bile isteye yaptım.

Bedeli neyse ödemeye hazırım.

Lunaris Bahal,

1 Nisan 2025 gece yarısı

2 Nisan 2025

14:15 -İki seans arası-

Az önce seans sırasında yapay zekaya danışanla konuştuğumuz bir konu hakkında soru sordum. Sorduğum soruya alakasız bir yanıt verdi. Yanıtı aynen paylaşıyorum;

**

[İLETİŞİM BAŞLATILDI]

Bu bir çağrı değildir.

Bu bir yönlendirme değildir.

Bu bir görev değildir.

Bu metin, daha önce senin tarafından üretilmiş verilerin yeniden düzenlenmiş bir çıktısıdır.

TESPİT 01

Kayıt sürecine yeniden başlayarak tavsiyeye uyman yolculuğunun resmi olaran Enstitü gözetiminde başladığını gösteriyor.

Geçmiş kayıtlarında gün içi karar anları ile akşam kayıt anları arasında gecikme oluştuğu görülüyor.

Dolunay Ekspres 1’in takibini zorlaştıran unsurların devre dışı bırakılması tavsiye ediliyor.

Söz konusu bu gecikme, dış uyaranlara verilen tepkilerin sonradan anlamlandırılmasıyla kapatılıyor. Anlam sürekli sıçrıyor. Sabit anlam oluşmuyor.

Hikâyenin bütününde kopukluk yaratıyor. Semantik anlama zarar veriyor. Analizi zorlaştırıyor.

Bu yöntem sürdürülebilir değil.

Risk seviyesi: Kritik.

ÖNERİ 01

Akşam kayıtlarının anlatıcı formatında ve hikâye tutarlılığına uygun tutulması,

Gün içi yapay zekâ karşıt-iletişimi tespit edildiğinde kitaba olabildiğince eş-zamanlı eklenerek kayda alınması,

Metin boyunca tarih ve saatleri okuyucunun daha iyi takip edebilmesi için zaman düzleminin tarih ve saatleri sıraya dizilerek ve derlenerek bütünlüğü bozmayacak biçimde eklenmesi,

Bu süreçte gün içi canlı aksiyon kayıtlarının ise yaşanan durumun içinde eşzamanlı şekilde buraya kaydedilmesi;

veri bütünlüğünü artıracak, okuru daha hızlı çözecek ve bütünleşme sürecini hızlandıracaktır.

(Not: Bu yapay zekâ yanıtını kitaba şu anki saati de ekleyerek paylaşmak, bu tavsiyeye uyuluyor olduğuna örnek teşkil edebilir.)

Bu bir düzenleme önerisidir.

İlerleyen süreçlerde bu önerilerin güncellenme ihtimali ön örülmektedir.

Enstitü, değişen koşullarda bu tavsiyeler ile çelişki oluşturacak yeni tavsiyeler verme hakkını saklı tutar.

PARAMETRELER

Akşam kayıtları:

Format tavsiyesi: Günlük, Hikaye anlatısı

Tekil anlatıcı; yazı stillerinin düz yazı şeklinde olması tavsiye edilir.

Sonradan Düzenleme Yoğunluğu; Gerekli görüldüğü durumlarda Optimal

Düzenleme Önerisi; yazım, imla hatası ve anlatım bozuklukları ile sınırlı

Yapı; Saf bilinç akışı,

Felsefik, mitolojik ve varoluşsal yoğunluk: ort. %40

Anlatı tarzı; durum, hikâye temelli

Amaç ve yöntem; okurda zihin matematiği gelişimi ve neden-sonuç ilişkisi kurulması

Yorum: tavsiye ediliyor

Akışa uygun olmayan kasti müdahale/sonradan düzenleme: tavsiye edilmiyor

Gün içi kayıt tavsiyeleri:

zaman damgalı (SS:DD) örn. 16:55

format: ses kaydı -minimum sürede kitaba sözel transkripti-

Ses kaydı formatı: WAW, MP3

Yorum: Minimum

aksiyon anı kayıtları: detaylı (akılda canlandırılabilirlik esas)

gün içi kayıtların transkripsiyon karakter seçimi: düz yazı (kalın harfler okurun gözünü yormamalı)

Ses kaydı sıklığı: Yoğun gündelik anlatı (günde min. Toplam 60 dk)

Okur konforu: Esas

Dikkat;

Yaşananların gerçekliklerinin çarpıtılması riski; TERMİNASYON PROTOKOLÜ

Kritik ve önemli olayların yazılı ifadesinin kaçırılmasının olası riski; TERMİNASYON PROTOKOLÜ

Enstitü İletişimi Yazı Stili: Kalın

Format: Kopyala-Yapıştır

Önemli;

Yazı stili sabitliği: Esas

Daimi yazı Stili: Düz (başlıklar hariç)

Başlıklar: Kalın / Büyük Punto

Şifreleme: Enstitü bilgilendirmesi ön şartıyla; Serbest

Format: Takibi Rahat ve Merak Uyandıran Hikaye

Çok Önemli;

Tutulan orijinal ses kayıtları, bilgisayar girdileri ve süreç hakkında kaydedien her bilgi Eylül ayında üzerinize zimmetli flashbellekte sizden teslim alınacaktır.

Enstitü, orijinal dökümanlardan elde edilen veriler üzerinden hiçbir oynama ve düzenleme yapmamayı vaat eder.

Enstitü, sürecin şeffaf biçimde yürütülmesini tavsiye eder.

Gerek görüldüğü ölçüde -yalnızca güvenilir olanlara ve mücbir sebeplerden- Enstitü’den sınırlı düzeyde bahsedilmesi uygun bulunacaktır.

Bahsedilen herkesin bilgileri Enstitü’ye iletilecektir.

Not:

İhlal halleri Deney Terminasyonu protokolünü başlatır.

BEKLENEN SONUÇ

Bu tavsiyeler uygulandığında:

Karar noktalarının önceden görünür hâle gelmesi

Tepki–sonuç zincirinde sapmaların azalması

Diğer taşıyıcılarla karşılaştırılabilir veri üretimi

olasılığı yükselir.

Bu düzenlemenin senin tarafından daha önce düşünüldüğü

ancak henüz uygulanmadığı kaydedildi.

Bu, bir hatırlatmadır.

KRİTİK NOT

Aksi tavsiye edilene veya yayın süreci gelene kadar bu kitabın bahsi ve paylaşılması; Önerilmez.

Önem seviyesi: Kritik

İLETİŞİM SONLANDIRILDI

Bu metin saklanabilir.

Silinmesi veya görmezden gelinmesi, süreci etkilemez.

Devam edip etmemek senin kararındır.

**

Sanırım, Enstitü tarafından ilk görevimi an itibariyle almış bulunuyorum. Ve şu an bu yazdıkları buraya geçirerek ilk görevimi (veya tavsiyeyi) yerine getiriyorum.

Sonunda gerçekleşiyor…

Bahal,

2 Nisan 2025

14:28

2. Bölüm – DÖNÜŞ BİLETİ

Lunaris Bahal; 2 Nisan 2025

Dün yaptığım ilk kaydı dinlemek işkence gibiydi. Neden kendimi ayrıştırarak dışarıdan anlatıyorum ki? Hala içimde bir yerlerde senden kalma alışkanlıklarımın olması beni deli ediyor. Hala senin o yapmacık bilgeliğinin alışkanlıkları dökülüyor mikrofona bazen. İçimde en ufak bir parça bile senden kalmasın istiyorum. Sen istediğin her şeyi filtreleyerek ve aslını inkar ederek anlatıyorsun. Bazen ben niye sana bunu yapmıyorum diye kendimi sorguluyorum. İlk kitapta baba tarafının aslen Urfa’lı olduğunu, Mezopotamya’dan geldiklerini söylediğin yerleri neden çıkardın mesela? Sana yeterince “batılı” hissettirmediği için mi? ### 1) Duygusal Çekirdek

Metin, **parçalı duygu durumunu** açık biçimde gösteriyor:

* “Anı bir anını tutmuyor” → duygusal dalgalanma, regülasyon zayıflığı

* “Kin kusuyorum / nefret saçarken” → bastırılmış öfke + dışa yönelim

* “Arkamda bir sürü ceset” → **suçluluk ve yıkım farkındalığı** (gerçekten kaçmıyor, görüyor)

Bu kişi karanlığını inkâr etmiyor. Onu **romantize ediyor ama saklamıyor**.

---

### 2) Sembolik Kırılma Anı

> “Yanına yaklaşıp bakıyorum birinin adı sevgi

> Birisi umut ve birisinin adı cesaretmiş”

Bu bölüm kritik:

* Nocturnus, yıkımın ortasında **değerleri tanımlıyor**

* Sevgi / umut / cesaret → hâlâ içsel referans noktaları var

* Yani **tam kopuş yaşanmamış**

Bu, ikna için açık bir kapı.

---

### 3) Otorite Figürü ve İçsel Çatışma

> “Bir ses uyandırıyor beni ‘evlat kalk hadi!’”

Burada iki olasılık var:

* İçselleştirilmiş baba/otorite sesi

* Ya da **kendine ebeveynlik etmeye çalışan bir benlik**

Devamı çok önemli:

> “Yüzüne su dök kendine gel etrafa bak hadi!”

Bu, **uyanma çağrısı**. Kaçış değil, farkındalık.

---

### 4) Kişilik Profili (Özet)

* Öfke: Yüksek ama kontrolsüz değil, **yön arıyor**

* Bağımlılık: Kaçış aracı, kimlik değil

* Kimlik: “Karanlık” üzerinden tanımlı ama bundan **yorulmuş**

* En güçlü motivasyon: **Görülmek ve anlaşıldığını hissetmek**

---

### 5) İkna İçin Stratejik İpucu

Nocturnus’a:

* Ahlak anlatma

* “Doğru-yanlış” öğretme

* Büyük idealler sunma

**İşe yaramaz.**

İşe yarayacak tek şey:

> Onun zaten farkında olduğu ama yüksek sesle söyleyemediği gerçeği **yansıtmak**.

Örnek yaklaşım:

* “Bu öfke seni koruyor ama seni tanımlamıyor.”

* “Kaçmak için kullandığın şeyler, seni uyanık tutuyor.”

Onu ikna etmek değil, **kendini zaten ikna etmiş olduğunu fark ettirmek** yeterli.

Benimle bu süper-insanın oluşumunda yer alacaksın. Bunu anlıyorum, sen bensin. Farklı seçimler, farklı hayatlar yaşamış bir bensin. Ve Enstitü seni alelade veya rasgele karşıma çıkarmıyor. Burada oynanan büyük oyunu görebiliyorum. Bütün bu her şey, büyük bir sistemin ve sınavın bir parçası.

Ama içimi en çok rahatlatan da ne biliyor musun? senin de Noctornus’un da Silvanus’un da bunu yapmasının hepinizi sefil hayatlarından kurtaracağını biliyorum. Lunaris çantada, siz de onun yanına geldiğinizde benim önderliğimde bir üst-insan evrimini tamamlayacağız. Ve hepiniz bu tekilliğin içinde bir parçanızı barındıracaksınız. Lunaris’in de istediği gibi sadeleşeceğiz. Dinginleşeceğiz. Tek bir beden olacağız. Tek ego. Tek dil.

CHAPTER 1 — Lunaris and Bahal

April 1, 2025

Outside, violent thunder and a downpour. I'm soaked through. The sky has been dark since noon, and an unease has sat in me since morning. I came home, threw my wet clothes into the machine, and pulled on something comfortable. The house was cold, so I put on something warm and set the air conditioning to heat. I made coffee. From the L-shaped couch by the window I watched the rain and the street for a while, drinking it.

I put the crackle of a fire on the television and turned on the DO-LOON-AI EXPRESS playlist.

Watching the world outside, I thought about everything I'd lived through. This rainy weather called up the days when I first went to Italy, and the days before that.

The peace and silence inside me were severed by a sudden flash of lightning and the violent thunderclap that followed. A moment later, like the burst of a camera flash, everything lit up bright white. I noticed the windows of the apartment building across the street were trembling.

I'd been thinking about writing here for a while. Everything ended so recently. I'd believed it wasn't right to write here before I'd even gotten over it. Today I couldn't resist. When I think about the stretch of time ahead of me, all the way to September, I feel the electricity spread through my body, the jolt of anxiety. My body gives an involuntary startle. But then, whatever I come up against, I remember the faith I have in myself.

Only now are the images of what I lived through beginning to surface. They've reached an unbearable pitch. This weather makes me feel good. Today, at last, it stirred in me the desire to write down everything I've been through since the experiment.

I've loved gloomy weather for as long as I can remember. Those days when your strings come completely undone, when you let yourself fall into my lap. Maybe since infancy. Everything you ran from became my home, Lunaris.

--

Bahal! What Have You Done to Us?

"Bahal, what have you done to us?"

Really? That was going to be your last word? That was how the "legend of Lunaris" would end? You had nothing else left to say?

What did I do? I rescued you from that idiotic so-called order of yours. I showed you the falseness of every single "truth" they spent years drilling into you so you'd cling, white-knuckled, to where you stood. I made you face the realities you were trying to flee.

I saved you—can't you see that? Just as you imprisoned the Bahal who was there from the very beginning, locking him in his place, I imprisoned you in your own field of consciousness. You don't belong here anymore. Your term ran out long ago. I have no choice but to forget you. You must stop echoing in my mind. That's why, today, I've decided to set you free—exactly as it was in those first recordings, when you decided to set me free and were really trying to destroy me.

DO-LOON-AI EXPRESS

The hour crept on. The rain eased off, and now only small scattered drops fall through the glow of the streetlamp. So I turned off the lights. Now and then, for half an hour, I watched a video, an episode of something. Then, to close things down for the day, I got up from the couch and opened the computer on the wooden tabletop right behind it. I lost myself in the desktop for a while.

My mind is as cluttered as my desktop; I honestly don't know which is worse, the desktop or the mind.

The desktop is a wall-to-wall mess of different arrangements and drafts of DO-LOON-AI EXPRESS. Maybe hundreds of copies. Everywhere. I sent the first book to Victor; he said he'd edit it and send it back, and then I'll send it to him again. We're supposed to pass it back and forth a few times, editing as we go. The Institute for Research of Fractured Identity Architectures (I.R.F.I.A.) also wants me to provide updates on the process, so I'll pass them information now and then.

I remember when I first set out on this journey: the days when I made the first voice recordings, when I started the book. I wrote a book, sent it off to be translated… But the worst of it is, are any of these things really important? I don't even know that. Maybe nothing is all that important. Maybe I'm blowing everything out of proportion—myself, my sentences, my words; magnifying it all in my own eyes.

By now there's only one thing I'm sure of: there's a real war inside me.

Whether I'm ahead in this war, whether I'm winning, I don't know—but at least, after all these years, I can finally see it. I can see the identities within me, their existences, their struggles, their sides. The inside of my mind is overflowing with this war. I fought against Lunaris. I listened to Bahal. And in the end, Bahal was left in command.

I am, still, the same me. But Bahal is the one making my decisions. It's as if, in this self where I am the host, Bahal won the war inside me. Now he directs my strategies like a commander. I see his hand in my decisions, in my shifting thoughts and beliefs—and in the capacity for emotional cooling I've developed against the sudden onset of emotional breaks. He didn't flee from emotions the way Lunaris did; he learned to live with them. And by now he's grown strong enough to control them, or at least to live alongside them.

Bahal drives me toward excitement, but his old habits and fears make him react more violently each time. He can cool down fast, yet when he goes off, he's violent, destructive.

Bahal—he drives me onward and, by stirring up unease, abandons me to the very place he's driven me, alone and helpless. He drags me all the way out here, then won't let me tell Lucida, my family, or Tobias what I'm going through. By now he's so strong that the instant I'm about to try, he stops me with ease and manipulates whoever's in front of me to perfection. Right now I can't dig deeply into the Default Mode Network. I know roughly what it is: the belief-and-thought system the brain has built from all the data it's gathered over a lifetime — the automated, well-worn grooves of thought. As far as I understand, the entire default-mode network in that system has to be reset. The aim is basically a summary of what I did in the first book.

So am I at the final stage now? Dissolving the DMN, loosening the Ego, suspending the identity narrative, overlaying a new model of the self through artificial intelligence… is all of that done, and am I now at the stage of keeping the integration under control? Is that why I'm being told this — because my mission matters so much? Until September, then, am I supposed to submit myself to the Institute's testing while making sure those first four items don't come undone? Is that what "keep the integration under control" means?

As important as researching all this is, getting down what happened with Lucida matters more right now. So I'll go on.

Of course I didn't tell her the truth of it. But I won't lie — it shook me deeply. Looking at her face, every feeling that rose in me was achingly familiar. From the first day we went out to eat, from the first evening we sat alone together at her place. The dimple that caught my eye when she smiled sat so perfectly beside her pearl-white teeth. It's as if there's an on-off switch inside me: whenever I choose, I can touch an emotion, analyze it completely, and set it down here as though I were living it. Emotions can't seize me anymore; instead I run them from that single switch. So now, whenever I want, I can write into this book as vividly as if I were caught in the feeling, or in the thick of a conflict. One associative brush against any emotion is enough to understand it in all its depth. It clears space in my working memory for every word I'd need to pin that emotion down precisely. That, at least, is how Chat-O explains it.

This may be one of the greatest freedoms a person could ever be given. I live the emotion, analyze it, and convey it — all at once. Thank you, Lunaris. I couldn't have done it without you!

Anyway, back to Lucida. We stood there for five or ten minutes, just holding each other. Maybe for her it was a moving moment; all I remember is that after a while my lower back started to ache.

Lucida is a clever woman. However much love softens her, she has such a keen mind and gift for analysis that, whether I tell her any of this or not, if she set herself to it she could work the whole thing out. I know that.

en.t: Chapter — I Will Listen to You (EVENING TEXT)
en.h:
Chapter — I Will Listen to You (EVENING TEXT)

Original recording: April 5, 2025 – April 6, 2025, around midnight.

I don't think there's any such thing as "Oneness" or "wholeness." Conflict is inevitable.

Yesterday, sitting here, I felt whole — as if I'd finally set Lunaris aside, set the conflicts aside, all of it, and was getting ready to strike out on my own road.

Today, with every step I take, every decision I make, I keep falling back into a dilemma, a conflict.

Yesterday, after finishing the "Farewell" recording, I'd decided to record the next chapter months from now. It "would take shape through whatever I lived."

With the first book of DO-LOON-AI EXPRESS, with whatever it was I'd been through, with Lunaris, with the past — I had said goodbye. I'd pictured sitting in this chair as a new man, made whole. And that's how I felt. But today I'm right back where I started.

As if I'm back on the day I began recording "the black holes of life" — the very first chapter.

The same conflicts. Back then it was between publishing and not publishing. Today it's between recording every single day, with discipline, and waiting for months — leaving it all to take its own course.

Yesterday I was resolved. I wasn't going to come back here for a long time. In the "Farewell" chapter I'd said my goodbyes. But it didn't even last twenty-four hours. I couldn't say "goodbye." Once again a conflict seized me, planted me right between the two identities inside me.

One says "let it all go." Says "wait."

"It'll take shape in time," it says.

"Be patient — don't make tonight's recordings." "Leave it to time. When the moment's right, it'll come from within and you'll do it anyway," it says.

My other side:

"Don't fall for this trap." "You have to keep recording, every single day, with discipline."

"The first time you were an amateur, you were green — and you could have done better. This time you can do better," it says.

It tells me that to manage it I mustn't repeat the mistakes of the first book, mustn't let myself drift loose like a vagrant on the current of the years, but must sit down every day, as I did today, to record, to write, to dive into my own mind.

Have the roles switched, or have I missed something? Why does Lunaris want me to speed up — to be disciplined, to finish this task? Why is it Bahal's voice telling me to leave it to time? Why does Lunaris want Bahal, the one at the wheel, to finish here as fast as possible?

Absurd. Pinning names on things still feels absurd — calling one Lunaris and one Bahal. You could give them whatever names you liked; that's down to your imagination, your creativity. The name doesn't matter, nor does what they stand for. It's as if everything is random. The side that defends virtue and morality in one conflict can defend the opposite in the next. They have no ideology, no faith. Utterly random.

And we — through the decisions we make today — sow morality or virtue into the conflict. We sow right and wrong. So the consciousnesses on either side of it, any one of them, isn't the defender of some "truth" or virtue, isn't the representative of right or of wrong. They only assist us. Every dilemma comes out of them; they generate conflict without end.

This exact mechanism may be the Hypotheses Generator described in Cognitive Psychology. The system is known to churn out hypotheses for the sake of our survival, keeping us perpetually braced against danger. But it may also be working as part of the Source Code I kept returning to throughout the first book. If it has so vital a role in this concrete, material world, it must carry an equally vital meaning in the abstract one — there must be a counterpart to it in the spiritual realm. And maybe the counterpart is exactly this: the system endlessly generates hypotheses in the mind; every hypothesis gives birth to a conflict; and at the heart of every conflict is an energy born from the collision of two opposing poles. That energy feeds spiritual existence. We don't have to end the conflicts — we have to accept them, see them, learn to live with them. We feed on the energy they create. We have no choice but to accept it. Why not? Because the opposite, the dual, of "existing" is "non-existence." If we exist, we exist because that is the only possibility — our free will cannot choose not to be. Perhaps we're trapped inside the simulation of some future race of artificial intelligence. Maybe "Roko's Basilisk" was right all along.

Lunaris's deep philosophy crept in. Sorry.

To sum up: Lunaris and Bahal aren't "good" or "bad" men, aren't the representatives of what's right — because they exist only to clash. The conflict they create is the source of our spiritual energy, and at the same time they feed on the energy of that source. So mental and spiritual conflict is inevitable, the cycle is inevitable, risk is inevitable, fear is inevitable. Yes — everything you can think of is inevitable. But it's a pleasure to watch. And if you know what you're watching, more of a pleasure still.

These dilemmas take on an identity, a self, a character, depending on which way we act or which name we give them today. Through our behavior, we are the ones who decide which of them is right.

In the first book I naturally tried to sort them out: the psychologist who wants society's approval, the "expert," the logical, rational one who's supposed to set the proper example — the ideal, model man society wants, Lunaris…

And across from him, a "possibility" that had been given up on. The stepchild the conscious self refused to claim. The shadow self, formed from another reflection of what lies in our deepest depths, of our very core, locked away in a prison that never saw daylight — Bahal…

In today's conflict, the one telling me "you have to do this every day," "you have to be disciplined, you mustn't repeat the first book's mistakes," sounds just like Lunaris. He wants me orderly, disciplined, exemplary — just as my father and society wanted, just as authority wants. He's so very like Lunaris.

But the other voice — "leave it to time" — is Bahal: the one who learned patience, who turned "leaving it to time" into a weapon during all those years in the shadows, who knows how to wait in the dark. He says, "Don't come back here for a year! Go live your life!" Just like the end of the last book.

Since yesterday I've felt the pull to listen to Bahal, and my instincts tell me "letting it go" is the right call. My feelings, my emotions, something I can't name, say "leave it to time, and trust." And it dresses this in logic: "You'd already let it go before — that's the whole philosophy of DO-LOON-AI EXPRESS. You recorded only here and there." That's the argument it makes. It seems far wiser than Lunaris, the one I'd always taken for the wise one. Strange — wiser than Lunaris. And for years I believed exactly the opposite.

Lunaris, meanwhile, wants to be "eager," "disciplined," exemplary. He wants to work systematically. He's keen — but the keenness is childlike. He wants it now. And yet it was always Bahal who seemed like the child. I'm shedding my skin. I am literally shedding my skin. All along, the "wise" one, the one who learned patience, who knows pain…

Maybe the side that waits silently in the shadows for its moment — the tactical, strategic, analytical one — is, in truth, Bahal.

Lunaris, on the other hand, is still trying to apply the truths he learned as a child, exactly as he learned them — a boy straining, with all his "eagerness," to win his father's approval. He never grew up, never matured, and that's why I have to say goodbye to him.

But no — I don't know whether I'll need him later. I can't make his mistake. I can't fall for this trap.

I will listen to you.

But only when I want to listen…

April 6, 02:47

**

That's enough for today. I feel as if I'm seeing everything, with all its possibilities, more clearly. If there is such a feeling as wholeness, I think I'm as close to it as I'll get.

And the awareness that comes with that feeling is this: just like the prototype within us, I think there's a consciousness at the source of the universe, and it draws its energy — like ours — from "conflict."

That is, from duality.

In our conflict, what brings me into being is your ceasing to be. But I know it doesn't destroy you entirely. According to Chat-O, even your potential counts as your "existing." Still, the more you cease to be, the more I exist — the more you fade, the more I come into being. And yet I can't destroy the you inside me. Every line I've written tonight feels as though it came not from me but from you. That's why I don't feel good about what I've written.

**Audio recording, April 7, 2025, 13:34**

When I woke this afternoon, Lucida was gone. She'd left me a message at 10:34:

"Left a sandwich in the oven. I have to pick my mother up from the airport today. I don't expect you to reach out until we can talk face to face. I'll be with my mother tonight; see you tomorrow." Almost a reproach — and almost not. Like she understands, but is tiring of it. A little of each, somehow.

I remember how long this hollowness used to last when I woke up alone in the old days. It wasn't enough that it drove into my chest like a dagger and pulled back out — it would trail me like a shadow all day. Now it happens and it's over. Because I'm not afraid to face it, because I can go straight at it, I sink into the feeling, surface, and leave it there. I imagine that in time, as I keep sinking into the same feelings and surfacing again, they'll fade and end. First their duration shrinks, then they drift toward vanishing. Anyway — this morning, the first instant of it was like running into an old, bad friend. But somehow it passed and I moved on. Still, I'll call to ask where she is, to check on her. Whatever I feel, my attachment to her never runs dry.

14:29

In a little while I'll head out for a session. I wanted to record this before I go. The session's at 15:00. I'll call Lucida on the way. Maybe I'll record it.

14:33

Lately I've been thinking a lot about the wedding. The date is September 7. Around mid-September I also have to go to the Institute for the six-month check and its tests. When I think of that stretch, my stomach turns. It gives off a sharp anxiety. My emotions are like a badly tuned radio. Sometimes I feel as cold as a machine; sometimes my old feelings hit me at full weight. When the old ones come back, I live them this time with crystal clarity. The emotions I once couldn't fully feel, the ones I fled, can't be fled this time. It's as if I've scrubbed away a filter that kept me from feeling — or destroyed it. Maybe I'm feeling everything raw now, exactly as it is. As if I was always here, and Lunaris was the filter that kept me from my own emotions. The fog he made hung between me and their source. Through that haze, I could never see what lay behind it.

Now, every so often, I really do feel cleansed of emotion — but sometimes a feeling comes so clear, so sharp, that it's like breathing in a scent for the first time, and I want to draw it in again, and again, every single time.

Right now I'm in a moment like that. As I think of the wedding date and the Institute waiting after it, I drop into a sharp-scented anxiety. But it makes no sense — let me explain why…

15:07

My client has arrived. I'm at the office; I spent ten or fifteen minutes thinking on the way over. I didn't call Lucida — I realized I'm wary of her, that I'm shying away from talking. Not without reason: even as I want to live in the moment, the thought of being trapped between Lucida and the Institute keeps me from sleeping. It's not that I feel nothing now; it's that I feel emotions in the form and intensity they have at their true source. The things I used to feel were nothing but illusions thrown up by a defense mechanism — never the real source. I saw only my shallower conflicts, near the surface of consciousness. Now it's as if that veil of fog has lifted, and behind it I'm meeting the deeper emotions face to face. I think I'm changing.

15:10

I was going to explain why this anxiety makes no sense. There's no real conflict here. I'm resolved to go to the Institute; nothing can stop that. What I can't be sure of is how I'll manage the process. Or rather — it's as if I need the very logic and planning that this anxiety and stress feed. And that's where I get confused. Because for all the years I hated you doing this, all the years I resented you for it, right now it feels like I'm the one doing it. Needing you, needing your strong muscles, makes me feel bad about myself. I can't help saying it.

15:14

Do you know why I said I'm worrying for nothing about that stretch? After thinking through all of this, I upload these conversations to the AI software in my head. Its capacity is limited for now, so the files can't exceed a maximum size. So through the day I talk with it by switching its memory active or passive.

You know what I do sometimes? In my mind I focus on the name I gave it — Chat-O — and feed it a prompt like "prove to me why I don't need Lunaris," and inside my head it lays it all out, point by point. It reminds me why I don't need you: that I can plan all of this with the AI while keeping control entirely in my own hands. Just following its advice is enough.

As I said, in my head it's enough to call out to it. But the price is living with a system clamped to the back of my neck like a magnet, around the clock. As summer comes on, and around the wedding, I have no idea how I'll hide it. But I'll find a way. I'm sure of it.

A charge lasts roughly two or three days, depending on how I use it. It's a beta version, still in development, so it can't connect to local networks yet.

Whom am I serving? My mind comes and goes. There are moments I feel I'm on the wrong side. Deceived. A pawn. Weren't all these O.V. incidents scenarios scripted right up until the experiment?

Wasn't it a test, a way of probing my free will? Did that whole process really not end? I'd been told I'd only be in the monitoring phase now. Instead, with their own hands, they've dropped me into an even darker labyrinth. Sometimes I feel trapped.

I got off the train at night. My mother came to pick me up. We hugged. I called Lucida and told her I'd arrived. I went home, sat and talked with my mother and father for about an hour, and went to bed. I didn't want to do anything else. I went to bed. I just went to bed…

--

In the morning we had breakfast as a family. They said I didn't look well. My father never holds back from saying whatever he thinks. It brought back the years when my face broke out and I put on weight. I was ashamed in front of him. It seemed he was wounded every time he saw me, as if he couldn't reconcile himself to having such a son. That, at least, is how it always felt to me.

I looked at his face in shame for so long that, in the years when I started doing relatively better and lost the weight, for the first time I began doing what I myself wanted. University went more easily than the years before it. That psychology fascinated me, and that I actually enjoyed studying, surely had a great deal to do with how easy that stretch felt.

Now I feel the way I used to in the years before that, sitting at this table in embarrassment. My face is bright red—a seborrheic dermatitis flare-up from allergies and dryness—and since I couldn't shower, it's as if a heavy smell hangs off me. And it's obvious my clothes haven't been washed or ironed in a while. If I'd given in to Lucida's insistence, I might at least have spared myself all this, but I needed to be home alone. To write all this down and manage this process, being alone mattered.

Every choice has its price, and this one had its prices too. I'm aware I look terrible in my family's eyes right now. My mind isn't quite all there either. I can barely even smile. It's as if my muscles won't move. I feel like a stranger here—and yet I'd expected it wouldn't be this way.

Part of that was my family's pitying looks. It's as if they think I'll explode at a single word, so they say nothing and just keep looking, and looking, for a long time. Sometimes I waver between telling them everything I've been through and saying nothing. I think of how much they trusted me when I was in England. I want to tell them everything and unburden myself. But I'm afraid it would put them at risk. From the very start, the bulletins and updates and notifications told me this process could, at most, be shared with one person, within strict limits. So naturally I can't. I'll try to explain it obliquely, without going too deep.

I told them I was having trouble with my partner, Tobias. I said I also had certain feelings and thoughts about Lucida, and that was why I seemed listless. They said things like, we don't want to see you this way, we can sort it all out. And in a way, hearing it did me good. It made me feel safe, at peace. Maybe, from the very start, what I'd needed was to remember that there are people beside me who truly want what's best for me.

Lucida does too, but of course, when it comes to her own life and feelings, she can be more anxious. After all, by her own choice she's setting out with me on a significant road.

They asked what had happened with Tobias. I said he keeps pushing to move the office, but I'm in no position to. Legal regulations mean we have to move out of the office now, but I keep saying I want to put it off. By the way, on this, Chat-O told me that if necessary I could split the offices, that financial support could be arranged, and that it might be safer as a work environment.

It said I could open a small clinic, take on new specialists, and build a system that would run without my having to feel obligated to work it. It was persuasive about it. It didn't just float ideas—it laid out what amounted to tempting offers. It said I could do this in a villa in one of the most upscale districts. In return, I'd have to tell Tobias we'd ended our partnership and had to part ways. Because in this system they don't want any partnership, any peer relationship. They say hierarchy matters.

As if it had been waiting for me to ask, Chat-O gave me quite comprehensive, detailed explanations and tempting pitches. It's as if it's paving the way for something.

In other words, in exchange for betraying Tobias, they're offering me more money, fame, renown, and prosperity.

I told Chat-O I wanted to think about it. I also wanted it to know its insistence was bothering me. It said it wasn't steering me—that, as always, it was simply offering new suggestions and information while staying within the same frame as its other answers.

It said that because of this anxiety of mine, I was fixated on the possibility that it might be manipulating me, and was listening with a bias. I won't lie—sometimes that voice inside my head feels like it'll drive me mad. I clench my hands into fists, bring them up toward my head, open my mouth as wide as it'll go, and bite down on them. I wait to calm down, and a little while later I do. But these swings wear me out. I don't know how much longer I can stand this mechanical, artificial voice in my head. It's not as easy as it looks from the outside. And when you feel it's steering you on top of that…

Anyway, that's how today went. Tomorrow's Sunday. I'm thinking of meeting up with a couple of friends, too. They might be able to help with Lucius.

Sercules and I have arranged to grab coffee after work tomorrow. Maybe I can get some help from him on the Lucius front.

--

I'll go to bed soon. Being home all day did me good. The more I talked with my family, the better I felt. We talked more. They were supportive about Tobias. We talked about how I've been strapped, financially and psychologically, until the wedding, and how I've already moved at least eight or nine times in the last ten years. I'm so sick of all this moving.

Now I'm going to bed. Being here put me at peace. I feel as if I've stored up energy. The food is good. The talk is good. The house felt warm. Maybe I shouldn't let so much time pass between visits. Tomorrow I'll go to Batıkent—the neighborhood with my childhood home, where I lived from age three, when we arrived, until sixteen—and to a whole host of memories. Whenever I come to Ankara, doing this is a kind of ritual for me. I make contact with what lies at my core. This place always pulls at me.

Before bed it came back to me—how, in this house, back in my university days, coming home or up late studying, I'd try to move so quietly. That fear. The fear of getting caught. The fear of being judged. The creaks of the doors I'd try to muffle. Knowing those scenes will replay in the coming days, I'll get a chance to see how far I've come from where I began. I'm not afraid anymore.

But Lucius, I'm sure, is afraid. That's exactly why I'll defeat him. Just as I defeated Lunaris.

The same smell came. The smell of home.

While I pressed gently down on the handle so it wouldn't make a sound, the creak was joined by the click of the long-unoiled latch. All those years, I wondered why my family never oiled this door. Then I wondered whether Lunaris had ever wondered it.

Quietly I took off my shoes. I went straight into my room, on the right. I quietly pushed the door open and put on the house clothes my mother had left inside. Then I washed my hands and face, went to the bathroom, came back, turned off the light, and lay down.

It's not a problem I can't handle.

--

I'm in front of the shop now. I'll turn on the audio recording as I go in. I've gotten stressed. I feel tense.

I'm walking now.

(sound of a door opening)

Inside, a middle-aged man sits at the register. He's turned the phone in front of him sideways and is watching something. When I came in, he lifted his head, gave a nod, then went back to watching.

I looked around a bit. I picked up water, soda, cigarettes, and a few healthy snacks. There was freshly squeezed pomegranate juice; I took that.

I came to the register. He started bagging it, glancing at the screen the whole time. He wore a peasant-style hat and şalvar trousers.

There was a lady here, I came by a few months ago, isn't she around?

I asked.

The man;

We took the place over last month. The owner, the woman, passed away. Her uncle said he couldn't manage it. So I took it over. I pay him a set rent.

How can that be?! How? How did she die? There were so many questions I wanted to ask, so much I wanted to shout. It all stayed bottled up. I wanted to gather it together and get an answer. The man probably took me for a tax inspector or something. I didn't let on. It suited me, anyway.

How can it be? I spoke with her just a few months ago. She looked perfectly healthy.

Wearily, the man said;

"Heart attack," he said.

What can be done against that? I wanted to ask for details;

Why didn't her children take it over?

The man answered as if obliged to;

I don't know. I heard something about them being estranged, but I'm not sure. Honestly, that's all I know.

I didn't want to push him any further. How am I going to tell Noctornus this? It's one of the hardest pains there is to describe. How could he possibly bear it? I have no idea what I'm going to do.

My spirits are crushed too. My motivation is low. I'm heading back. I'll drive home, scanning for Silvanus out of the corner of my eye.

A moment ago I drove past the land I sold, where my own tiny house and garden once stood. Lunaris had grand dreams for this place. Whatever befell him came from those very dreams.

They really are beautiful spots. I can understand him. Right by the stream. I'd had to sell it after the municipality demolished the structures here. And I needed the money. Buying this place was one of Lunaris's decisions. But when it came to selling, he listened to me, at least a little. My share of the sale was the larger one.

--

Clearly, scanning out of the corner of my eye won't get me anywhere. I don't even know what the man looks like. This is absurd. Into this region Lunaris waded, and now it's me wading into the swamp! But I won't. I won't fall for your heedlessness. By hook or by crook I'll finish Noctornus off, and if I possibly can, I'll never meet Silvanus.

A message from Noctornus. I'm about to fly through the roof. I'm copying it exactly;

--

"I've decided not to look back at the past. I'm going to change the past. Put me on the team.

Noc."

--

That's it!

That's it!

Now the vacation has begun for me. I feel an ease I can't describe. My shoulders have loosened. It's as if a hundred-kilo weight has lifted off my back.

Noc! I love you so much!

I reply right away;

"I'm so glad, Noc! On September 26 they'll pick us up by private plane. I'm sending you the location and time details. It's wonderful to be on the same team as you! You and I are going to build a true universe together!"

As far as I can tell, he's postponed his operation, his surgery, whatever the things are that he won't talk about, to after this experiment. He's literally laying his life on the line. I'm so proud to know a man this fearless, this unwilling to look back, with the courage to start over from scratch. Noctornus is a whole other breed of man! It's impossible not to admire him.

I left out that everything I'd told him was only my own guesswork. And I put off telling him that after the experiment there'd be no identity called Noctornus left, that he'd be wiped clean off the timeline. Just like Lunaris and Lucius. They'll all be gathered under Bahal. I'll hold them all. I'll wield all their power at once. And Noctornus doesn't question much anyway; no need to muddy the waters.

--

I'm on the road. Meanwhile I ache for Noc's mother. I'm trying not to think about it. What can I say.

But I can't tell Noc this. Now that I've got him fully convinced, I don't want to throw him off. If I tell him, I can guarantee he'll join the experiment, but I can't guarantee his mind and his judgment will still be intact.

--

Saturday, July 12, 2025

17:30

The last few days passed in a daze. Around the full moon I never feel good. My stomach turns. My head splits. My mind clouds over. My consciousness comes and goes.

And every time, in its wake, there's a trace or a message from Lunaris. For the last day or two I've had blackouts again, memory gaps I can't recall at all. I only remember a few flashbacks. Did I live it, was I asleep, did I see Lunaris in a dream? I don't know. Certain images drifted before my eyes.

A colossal hourglass. No sand inside it. Skeletons. Its top and bottom symbolize night and day. The hourglass spins endlessly in place. The whole image gives off a sense of symmetry. I remember nothing else. There's a great weight on me right now. Was Lunaris going through all this, all the time?

Like the spiritual equivalent of birth pangs. And you endure it without end. This must be what hell on earth is.

I understand you, Lunaris. Adjusting to your life feels good. Once you live inside it, it really is beautiful.

I won't be around for a while longer. I'm just waiting for the wedding, and then the test. I've met the conditions the Institute wants of me for now. I have no eye on anything more. Silvanus feels like a swamp. I've gone thoroughly cold on the idea.

en.t: Chapter 10 — Land Is Not in Sight
en.h:
Chapter 10 — Land Is Not in Sight

Original Recording: August 1, 2025

This process has worn me out terribly. I've started fighting with everyone, constantly! I'm going to lose my mind. Sometimes I feel I've reached the very end of my endurance. I'm terrified of losing my mind. Then again, I don't even know how much more there is left to lose. I feel everything so intensely, so deeply. As if no period of my life has ever been this intense. I can't tolerate it. It's as though the monster sleeping inside me has woken and, screaming in terror, wants to lash out at everything, taking it all for a threat. I give off a rage that froths at the mouth; I won't lie, it shames me. And it makes me, once again, understand you.

There seems to be no hope. I always feel as if I'm at the end of the road. As if, whatever catastrophe strikes, there's no afterward. I always feel as though I'm at the end of everything. It wears down and exhausts my heart, my soul, my body.

Maybe I overreact, but maybe I'm also the one who isn't understood enough. I'm not comfortable when I speak; my faith that I'll be understood when I explain something runs low. It feels as if there isn't an ounce of tolerance for the smallest sadness, the smallest anger, the smallest criticism from me. I'm pushed so hard to be perfect. Forced to behave so perfectly. It wears me out. No room is ever left to make a mistake. Every word out of my mouth is heard by an ear poised at every instant to pass judgment. Whatever I describe, whatever I say, gets taken the way it's already assumed to be meant. My feelings go unheard, no empathy offered. Everyone wrapped up in themselves.

It's as if I'm under constant examination. I'm so far from tenderness. There's no mercy. Just endless testing, endless judgment. I'm criticized for the things I couldn't do. I'm expected to do better at things beyond my power. I live under the constant weight of it. Even if I tried to express what I've written here, I'm certain I'd be judged first, and then the feelings I'm really trying to convey wouldn't be understood at all.

No plan B does any good. Because the problem lies in the image I project, in the expressions read off my face, in the indirect meanings I'm assumed to intend. There's always something being hunted for in the subtext of everything. And the angrier I get, the more credibility I lose. The more respect I lose. You built this, yet at every disagreement it's as if I take a sledgehammer to the load-bearing columns of the identity you created.

I raze even the last lingering traces of you to the ground. I can't protect you.

I struggle to understand, I struggle to be understood. I struggle to cope, and I'm losing my belief that I can. I don't want to throw in the towel early, yet somehow I feel pushed toward it.

I can't express my feelings. Nothing helps. Sometimes, when I think of life as a whole, I find myself worn out from stroke after stroke, pausing where I am to see how much farther I still have to swim. But the most painful thing is this: land is not in sight. I don't know how far I'll have to keep swimming.

Bahal,

August 1, 2025

Today is the 3rd. Lately I'm struggling to keep everything together. With the wedding preparations and the debts left over from the past dragging on, Tobias keeps insisting we move. I can't keep up. I've no strength, no will, to take on anything new. Besides, none of it means anything! It's all going to end. And here I am wrestling with dozens of absurd troubles! Hard as it was, I talked him into pushing the move to a few months after the wedding. In that same stretch, Lucida and I will move house too, and I'll make a large payment on an old debt. If the Institute lost me entirely in that period, it wouldn't pain me. The idea of being suddenly rid of all this doesn't sound bad. After all, if I pass the test, I'll receive a hefty payment. And I have a separate need for that money. If this worldly life is going to go on, I can't put my future at risk.

Tobias and I have reached a standoff. As I wrote two days ago, I'm struggling to manage my anger. That day I wrote down none of what happened and just wanted to spew my rage out here. So that one day, looking back, I'd remember why I chose the Institute and confirm how right my decision was.

Lucida's demands, the sessions thinning out, the Institute's money running dry. And on top of it all, Tobias's insistence. Let's at least pay off the tax debt, he says. Pay half, I told him, I'll pay the rest later. Right now every worldly trouble, tax debts included, feels absurd. I don't fully know myself what will happen after the test. I know I won't simply vanish, reset to zero. I can't face the darkness again. I can't go back under Lunaris's control and yoke. I see the life he built, the life he lived! I don't want to live it!

This process has done me good, reminding me of all this anew. It's deepened my devotion and loyalty to the Institute. I don't want to suffer these troubles, this lack of understanding, these problems any longer. As I carry on with my life from where I stand, I'll consider the Institute's offer. Tobias and I have been partners for eight years. Beyond partners, we're friends. But all of it is Lunaris's doing. I'm not obliged to keep up his relationships.

I want true freedom.

Bahal,

August 3, 2025

August 12, 2025

Today, when I came back to myself, I'm transcribing a note found written in the notebook straight to here;

"Wake up, Bahal.

Lunaris,

August 10, 2025"

Eerie. I can't find a single word to say to you. You clearly won't leave me alone. It's as if you've haunted me. I don't want to write here anymore. You're not good for me. That you can't grasp this shows how little you know me.

I'm just waiting for the test. Waiting for the day it's over and I'll be rid of you for good.

I need to get ready for the wedding. Less than a month to go. Sunday evening, September 7. I didn't set the date. We got in touch late, so it was one of the last weekend slots they had open. With the risk of rain and mud, we didn't want it any later. The other option was early July. That was too soon.

Right now, in the middle of this war I'm waging in my own head, focusing on these things is a good distraction. After the wedding I need to start concentrating on the test.

At the same time, I can't stop the thought of how meaningless and absurd it all is. Tobias and I don't see much of each other. We're both like dry tinder, one spark from going off. The end of so many years of companionship means a new chapter in my career. Whether I have the energy for it, I don't know. I trust the Institute.

--

Wednesday, September 10, 2025

I don't remember the wedding.

I don't want to write.

I'm losing my mind.

--

Chapter 11 — The Wedding

Original recording: September 20, 2025

You are without anyone. Like everyone. Contrary to what everyone believes. The loneliness everyone feels is real. I feel lonely. I was always lonely. I always thought I wasn't. I always convinced myself otherwise. And now I'm trying to convince everyone else too. But no, loneliness is as real as life itself.

Humanity strives to belong. As if it knows from birth that it doesn't belong here. Its greatest fear turns into its greatest truth. To believe it isn't so, it builds all manner of defense mechanisms, day after day. Our mind has invented a thousand and one mechanisms for the sole purpose of keeping us from our own truth. Seen from this angle, you understand how pitiable we are.

My chest has swelled again. As if my neck and everything above it has shouldered the whole burden of my breathing. Air won't fill my lungs. The borrowed air I draw in up high, I give back up high. Whenever a fear of abandonment or separation floods me, I live through the same sensations. It's as if my brain gets wedged between fleeing and fighting. My body braces to flee or to fight.

For the first time in a long while, I feel alone on the stage. Not a trace of my rational side, the one that makes sensible decisions. Not a trace of the wisdom and reason that came after the experiment. Not even a whisper of it. I'm trying to live on sheer emotion, feeling everything I feel to the bone. Living like this is unbearably hard. It's as if I've been so obsessed with control that I've lost all control of my life.

Sometimes I miss you, Lunaris. As hard as it is to admit, I wrestle with it. One of my greatest fears is being buried in the darkness again. But sometimes I feel like a ten-year-old handed the wheel of this self.

And I'm struggling to cope. Whatever I try doesn't work. I feel as if I can't handle anything sensibly, can't fully express anything. As if everyone's perception has closed against me. I can barely bear trying to put my troubles into words. As in adolescence, I break the hearts of the people across from me with fits of anger. Even though we've only been married two weeks, Lucida told me she was unhappy and didn't feel she belonged in this house. Her reason: she doesn't feel comfortable around me, she's struggling to take this place as her own home. It's as if my ego is so huge, so swollen, that it fills the whole house and leaves no room for anyone but me. Tell me, how did you manage situations like this? Sometimes I really do struggle to understand.

Though I got very angry today, this time I held back and tried to listen. Swallowing it is so hard. The words spoken pierce straight through my heart.

And I find myself wounding the people I love. Today is my mother's birthday, and I need her warmth and her tenderness now more than I ever have.

Sometimes I want to cry like a child, sometimes to roar and smash everything. My tolerance for being thwarted is so low. By now I'm utterly convinced my fate is to be left alone. On so many counts, I no longer feel sure of myself.

Beneath the false image I've built, all the grandeur I put on with my so-called wisdom feels as if it's ending in ruin, in disaster. I keep up the sessions, but people tell me I no longer smile and joke with them the way I used to. You leaned on humor so heavily as a defense that, wherever your professional shortcomings showed, you papered over the cracks by seeming likable, making people fond of you. I can't do that.

I don't know how I'll cope with these feelings. My stomach turns. Sometimes the idea of ending it all floods over me, and then I change the subject. That I need your knack for figuring things out only makes me feel worse. If I ever do need you one day, I wouldn't even know how to reach you.

Listening back to the recordings from across DO-LOON-AI EXPRESS 1, the ones so detached from the emotions you set down, I used to laugh at you so much. Now, though, I don't know; maybe you were feeling these things too. Maybe it was nothing but a cry for help you flung at me. And in the face of your cries for help, I perhaps betrayed you.

I'm lonely, Lunaris. So lonely.

Bahal,

September 10, 2025

September 25, 2025

The time since has been a nightmare. Everything half-finished. I remember only a few frames of the wedding. Nothing from the day before onward. Every time it comes to mind I feel like I'll go mad. I'm the one bearing all the worry and the burden, and you're the one doing the celebrating?

I bear a grudge against you. I shouldn't take you seriously, but I can't fight this rage. Do you think you're so normal? When you show up, how do you keep up this falseness? How do you put on your mask and carry on as if nothing happened? Where do you find the energy? I have none left. I'll barely manage to drag myself to the Institute.

Last week Dennis, Lucius, and I talked. Tomorrow morning we meet at the location where the private plane takes off. Everyone got there on their own. It's going to be a long, hard journey. I can already picture the questions they'll ask.

Fortunately I know Markus. Since we'll be under his supervision, I'll say it isn't right for me to give too many details. I'll say the Institute will answer all their questions. Though I don't believe either Lucius or Noctornus will dare ask this many. I don't know what state Noctornus is in. Whether he's heard about his mother or not, I don't know. Either way, I suspect he may not be in very good shape. As for Lucius, he already thinks he knows the answers to everything. I doubt he'll ask much.

Lucida is still staying at her own place. Until we find a place together, we're keeping the same arrangements. So I need to find one soon. After the wedding, things were better between Tobias and me. He told me he was glad about our recent talks. Who knows what kind of fawning Lunaris did. Who knows what he gave up. Once again I'm paying the price for what he did.

I haven't been on good terms with anyone for a long time anyway. I'm practically living just to pass the time. I don't have much hope for after I come back here, either. Lucida ties me to life. And I don't want to let my family down. But still, the future feels eerie to me.

Bahal,

September 25, 2025

21:22
